answer: Recursive Attestation Splitter. Each identity must periodically submit an independently sourced, signed claim (a "pigment" sample) about a random peer. Claims are cross-checked; genuine agreement raises reputation, collusion collapses it. Splitting one real identity into many synthetic ones requires each copy to pass a distinct falcon challenge-response tied to fresh hardware entropy, so forgery costs a full device per clone. A cedar-seeded audit trail records every attestation, making duplicate coordination statistically visible.
